title: Unify the three money-text parsers and two short formatters in lib/format
body:
## Summary
Typed amounts are parsed by three implementations and shortened by two, and they disagree on edge inputs.

## Description
parseMoneyText (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts:33), parseAmount (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/ladder.ts:111) and parseMoneyInput (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/model.ts:22) each parse owner-typed money; fmtShort (counter/model.ts) and short (tables/ladder.ts:20) each drop ".00"; minorToText and toInput each render the editable text; counter currencyMark duplicates lib/format currencyMark. Divergences today: counter accepts "58." and "$ 58" and rejects 10+ digit amounts, the other two do not; after this round's comma fix (a7ab89a) the approval copy still reads "340,50" as 34,050. Registry status-vocabulary/number-formatting: one primitive owns the rendering so no call site re-decides it. Fixed = one parser, one short formatter and one input renderer in lib/format.ts, the three callers importing them.

## Flow
- build a table-driven test over ~12 inputs ("58", "58.", "$ 58", "58,50", "1,058", "12345678901", "0.1", JPY "5.5") run against all three parsers; it shows the divergent rows
- move one parser + formatter into lib/format.ts with the comma rule; re-point counter/model, tables/ladder, approval/model
- the table test now runs one implementation; keep the per-module tests

## Expected impact
An owner gets the same verdict on a typed price in the Counter, the Tables ladder and the approval window. Could break: approval-window inputs that relied on "58." being refused.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for typed money instead of three that disagree
Before: 3 parsers, 2 short formatters, 2 input renderers, 2 currencyMark; >=4 inputs parse differently between them (walked: "58.", "$ 58", "58,50" vs approval, 10-digit)
After: 1 of each (predicted); 0 divergent rows in the table test
Method: simulation - four inputs walked through the three bodies; the seam spans lib/format and the approval window, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts:33 parseMoneyText
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/ladder.ts:111 parseAmount
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/model.ts:22 parseMoneyInput (byte-identical to ladder's pre-a7ab89a body)
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/format.ts:15 currencyMark vs apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts:24 currencyMark
instrument: a table-driven vitest over the 3 parsers with ~12 inputs, red on any row where they disagree; then the same test over the single lib/format parser

title: Move the ladder and floor model sentences into the area words files and guards
body:
## Summary
About 30 user-facing sentences live in the pure models, outside lib/words and outside the area words guards.

## Description
UX-GUIDE checklist: "Strings live in lib/words.ts or the area's lib/words/<area>.ts, and the area's words guard passes". apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/ladder.ts consequences() (~13 sentences), standLine() (4), diffLines/LIMIT_WORD (3) and apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts vsMarket() (7) and floorError() (3) render on Layer 1 (the what-changes sheet, the stand line, the price list) but the guards in tables.test.tsx / counter.test.tsx walk only TABLES/COUNTER via wordsOf, so a vendor name or raw state in these sentences would pass. Fixed = the sentences as functions in lib/words/tables.ts and counter.ts, the models calling them, the guards covering them for free.

## Flow
- extend each area guard with the model outputs on fixed inputs (instrument) and seed a forbidden word in consequences() to watch it pass today
- move the sentences into the TABLES / COUNTER words objects (shared surface: one commit)
- re-point the models; ladder.test/model.test keep their exact-text assertions

## Expected impact
The words guard covers every sentence the Tables and Counter areas say. Could break: exact-text tests if a sentence is reworded in the move (do not reword).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every Layer-1 sentence of the two areas under the words guard
Before: ~30 sentences in 2 model files, 0 covered by the area words guards (wordsOf walks only the words objects)
After: 0 sentences outside lib/words; all covered (predicted)
Method: simulation - counted the template literals in consequences/standLine/diffLines/vsMarket/floorError; the move touches lib/words (shared) and both models, M, beyond this round's S budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/ladder.ts:166 consequences()
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/ladder.ts standLine()
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/counter/model.ts:137 vsMarket()
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/tables/tables.test.tsx guard walks TABLES/TABLES_TRADE/TABLES_VIEWS only
instrument: guard extension: run consequences()/standLine()/vsMarket()/floorError() on fixed inputs through the same regexes; seed "Rust" into one sentence -> must go red

title: Take the band-movable states from approval gating instead of a second copy
body:
## Summary
The Tables ladder keeps its own copy of the states in which a price range may still move.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/tables/Ladder.tsx:25 BAND_MOVABLE = {PAIRING, LISTED, NEGOTIATING}, commented "approval/gating.ts BAND_MOVABLE"; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/gating.ts:66 holds the one the approval window enforces (it also requires kind haggle, :206). apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/tables/groups.ts:9 OPEN repeats the same three states for a different rule. Nothing asserts the two BAND_MOVABLE sets agree: if gating changes, the ladder offers a drag the approval window refuses (or hides one it allows). Fixed = gating exports a bandMovable predicate and the ladder imports it.

## Flow
- add a test asserting Ladder movable === gating band_set admission over every DealState for a haggle (instrument)
- export the predicate from approval/gating.ts, import it in Ladder.tsx, delete the copy

## Expected impact
The ladder shows a draggable limit exactly when the approval window will take it. Could break: nothing visible today (the sets are equal).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source for when a band may move
Before: 2 hand-kept copies of the band-movable states, 0 tests tying them
After: 1 source, imported; the parity test pins it (predicted)
Method: simulation - the sets are equal today, so no behaviour differs to probe; the seam is approval/gating.ts, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: for every DealState, Ladder movable equals gating band_set admission for a haggle; seed a state removed from one copy -> red
